discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms entangled via Rydberg interactions, for quantum simulation and computation

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: The nominees turned single neutral atoms, held one by one in optical tweezers, into a programmable quantum platform. Saffman and Browaeys were the first to demonstrate the Rydberg blockade between two individual atoms and to use it to produce entanglement and quantum gates. This realised the proposal that Lukin and collaborators had made. Browaeys and Lukin then built defect-free, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms. With these arrays they simulated quantum magnetism and observed exotic phases, including quantum many-body scars and topological spin liquids. Lukin's group went on to demonstrate logical qubits with error correction. This is the second quantum revolution in its purest form: entanglement between individually controlled particles, once a subject for gedankenexperiments, has become a precise tool for exploring many-body physics and for building quantum processors.
